question:
Read the following statements carefully and select the correct option regarding their correctness.
Statement I: ‘Project Tiger’ is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) of the Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change.
Statement II: The National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) has been fulfilling its mandate of strengthening tiger conservation in the country within the ambit of the Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972. (RPF Constable 2024 (17/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Statement I is incorrect, while Statement II is correct.
Statement I is correct, while Statement II is incorrect.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

Explanation:
Project Tiger was launched in 1973 as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) under the Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change. Its goal is to protect tigers and their habitats. The National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) was established under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. It works to strengthen tiger conservation in India by managing tiger reserves, preventing poaching, and conserving habitats. Thus, both statements are accurate.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ Which ministry administers Project Tiger? → Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change
☛ What does NTCA stand for? → National Tiger Conservation Authority
☛ Under which act was NTCA constituted? → Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972
☛ Which scheme is a CSS for tiger conservation? → Project Tiger

question: Which of the following rivers is an antecedent river that originates north of Mount Everest in Tibet, where its main stream, the Arun, rises? (RPF Constable 2024 (17/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Gandak
Kosi
Son
Gomati
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Kosi

Explanation:
The Kosi river is an antecedent river that originates north of Mount Everest in Tibet. Its main stream is the Arun, which is part of the Saptakoshi river system. The Kosi is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar' due to the widespread devastation caused by its floods. It is one of the major rivers originating from the Himalayas and carries a heavy sediment load, causing frequent changes in its course. Gandak is also an antecedent river, but it does not originate north of Mount Everest; its source is in Nepal. Son is a river of central India, and Gomati is a tributary of the Ganges. Hence, Kosi is the correct option.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Origin of Kosi river → North of Mount Everest in Tibet
☛ Main stream of Kosi river → Arun
☛ State most affected by Kosi floods → Bihar
☛ Nickname of Kosi river → Sorrow of Bihar
☛ Type of river Kosi is → Antecedent river
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सी नदी एक पूर्ववर्ती नदी है जो तिब्बत में माउंट एवरेस्ट के उत्तर में निकलती है, जहाँ इसकी मुख्य धारा, अरुण, निकलती है? (RPF Constable 2024 (17/03/2025) Shift 3)

कोसी
सोन
गोमती
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है कोसी

Explanation:
कोसी नदी एक पूर्ववर्ती नदी है, जो तिब्बत में माउंट एवरेस्ट के उत्तर से निकलती है। इसकी मुख्य धारा अरुण है, जो सप्तकोसी नदी प्रणाली का हिस्सा है। कोसी को 'बिहार का शोक' भी कहा जाता है क्योंकि बाढ़ आने पर यह व्यापक तबाही मचाती है। यह हिमालय से निकलने वाली प्रमुख नदियों में से एक है और अपने साथ भारी मात्रा में गाद लाती है, जिससे नदी का मार्ग बार-बार बदलता है। गंडक भी पूर्ववर्ती नदी है, लेकिन यह तिब्बत में माउंट एवरेस्ट के उत्तर से नहीं निकलती; इसकी उत्पत्ति नेपाल में है। सोन मध्य भारत की नदी है और गोमती गंगा की सहायक नदी है। इसलिए कोसी ही सही विकल्प है।

question: In which of the following Indian states is the primitive form of cultivation (slash and burn agriculture) called ‘Bewar’ or ‘Dahiya’? (RPF Constable 2024 (17/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Uttar Pradesh
Karnataka
Kerala
Madhya Pradesh
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Madhya Pradesh

Explanation:
Slash and burn agriculture is known by different names in different Indian states. In Madhya Pradesh, it is called Bewar or Dahiya. This primitive farming method involves cutting and burning forest trees to clear land for cultivation. After a few years, when the soil fertility declines, farmers move to another area. Other states have different names: in Andhra Pradesh it is known as Podu, in Bihar as Salma, in Rajasthan as Valtra, and in the northeastern states as Jhum. This practice is harmful to the ecosystem, and the government has taken measures to control it.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ Which state is Jhum cultivation prevalent in? → Northeastern states
☛ What is it called in Andhra Pradesh? → Podu
☛ What is the local name for slash and burn in Bihar? → Salma
☛ What is it called in Rajasthan? → Valtra

Explanation:

question: Chilika Lake, the largest brackish water lagoon in India, is located in which state? (RPF Constable 2024 (17/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Odisha
Tamil Nadu
Andhra Pradesh
Kerala
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Odisha

Explanation:
Chilika Lake is the largest brackish water lagoon in India, located in the state of Odisha. It is a shallow lagoon connected to the Bay of Bengal, with an area varying seasonally between 900 to 1,165 sq km. Chilika is a vital habitat for migratory birds and hosts several endangered species. It was designated as a Ramsar site in 1981 to protect its rich biodiversity. The lake supports local fisheries and tourism, playing a crucial role in the economy of coastal Odisha. It is situated on the eastern coast of India, near the towns of Puri and Ganjam.

question: Who is known as the ‘Father of the Green Revolution’ in India? (RPF Constable 2024 (17/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: MS Swaminathan
Norman Borlaug
Jawaharlal Nehru
Verghese Kurien
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is MS Swaminathan

Explanation:
The Father of the Green Revolution in India is Dr. M. S. Swaminathan. He introduced high-yielding varieties of wheat and rice in the 1960s, making India self-sufficient in food grain production. Norman Borlaug is globally recognized as the father of the Green Revolution, but in India, Swaminathan's role is unique. Verghese Kurien is known as the father of the White Revolution, and Jawaharlal Nehru was India's first Prime Minister. Swaminathan connected farmers with modern agricultural techniques and ensured food security.

question: In which state is the wettest place on the earth 'Mawsynram' located? (RPF Constable 2024 (17/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Mizoram
Meghalaya
Kerala
Manipur
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Meghalaya

Explanation:
The wettest place on Earth, Mawsynram, is located in the state of Meghalaya, India. It receives an average annual rainfall of about 11,872 millimeters (467 inches). Mawsynram is situated near Cherrapunji, which previously held the title of the wettest place. Meghalaya means 'abode of clouds', reflecting its climate. The region lies in Northeast India and experiences heavy rainfall due to monsoon winds. The main reason for Mawsynram's high rainfall is the moisture-laden winds from the Bay of Bengal that are blocked by the Khasi Hills, causing orographic rainfall.

question_hi: पृथ्वी पर सबसे नम स्थान 'मावसिनराम' किस राज्य में स्थित है? (RPF Constable 2024 (17/03/2025) Shift 3)

मेघालय
केरल

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है मेघालय

Explanation:
पृथ्वी पर सबसे नम स्थान मावसिनराम भारत के मेघालय राज्य में स्थित है। यह स्थान अपनी अत्यधिक वर्षा के लिए प्रसिद्ध है और यहाँ औसत वार्षिक वर्षा लगभग 11,872 मिलीमीटर (467 इंच) होती है। मावसिनराम, चेरापूंजी के पास स्थित है, जो पहले सबसे नम स्थान माना जाता था। मेघालय का अर्थ है 'बादलों का घर', जो यहाँ की जलवायु को दर्शाता है। यह क्षेत्र पूर्वोत्तर भारत में आता है और मानसूनी हवाओं के कारण यहाँ भारी वर्षा होती है। मावसिनराम की वर्षा का मुख्य कारण बंगाल की खाड़ी से आने वाली नम हवाएँ और खासी पहाड़ियों का अवरोध हैं।

question: The sand dunes in the Thar desert are primarily formed by: (RPF Constable 2024 (18/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: river erosion
flash floods
wind action
earthquakes
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is wind action

Explanation:
The sand dunes in the Thar desert are primarily formed by wind action. This is an arid region with sparse vegetation and strong winds. Wind transports sand particles from one place to another, depositing them to form dunes of various shapes. The main types of sand dunes are barchans, seifs, and parabolic dunes. Barchans are crescent-shaped dunes. Wind direction and speed play a crucial role in dune formation in the Thar desert. Processes like river erosion, flash floods, and earthquakes are not the primary agents in the formation of desert dunes.

question:
Which region of the Western Coastal Plains is known for its indented coastline with
natural harbours? (RPF Constable 2024 (18/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Konkan Coast
Malabar Coast
Karnataka Coast
Gujarat Coast
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Konkan Coast

Explanation:
The Western Coastal Plains are divided into three sections: Konkan Coast, Karnataka Coast, and Malabar Coast. Among these, the Konkan Coast extends from Mumbai to Goa and is known for its indented coastline and natural harbours such as Mumbai, Marmagao, and Nhava Sheva. The coastline features numerous creeks, bays, and estuaries, making it ideal for port development. The Karnataka Coast is relatively less indented, while the Malabar Coast is long and straight. In the Konkan region, the Western Ghats approach close to the sea, resulting in short, swift rivers that create many rias and estuaries, further contributing to the rugged coastline. This unique topography provides excellent shelter for ships, making it a region rich in natural harbors.

question:
Which of the following was a significant problem faced by the agricultural sector in
India around 1947? (RPF Constable 2024 (18/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: High productivity levels
Dependence on monsoons
Modern farming techniques
Surplus production
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Dependence on monsoons

Explanation:
At the time of independence in 1947, Indian agriculture was primarily rain-fed and heavily dependent on monsoons. There was a lack of irrigation facilities, leading to erratic crop production. Natural calamities like droughts and floods severely affected farming. High productivity, modern techniques, and surplus production were not possible because agricultural practices were traditional and underdeveloped. Before the Green Revolution, India was not self-sufficient in food grains.

question: What was the primary characteristic of the Indian economy on the eve of independence in 1947? (RPF Constable 2024 (18/03/2025) Shift 2)

agriculture.

It had a well-developed banking and financial system.

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is It was primarily an agricultural economy with most of the population dependent on agriculture.

Explanation:
At the time of independence in 1947, the primary characteristic of the Indian economy was that it was predominantly agricultural. Thus, the main feature of the economy was heavy dependence on agriculture and backwardness.

question: Which geological event led to the formation of the Peninsular plateau? (RPF Constable 2024 (18/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Collision of tectonic plates
Glacial activity
Breaking and drifting of Gondwana land
Volcanic eruptions
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Breaking and drifting of Gondwana land

Explanation:
The Peninsular plateau of India was formed by the breaking and drifting of the Gondwana land. This geological event occurred during the Mesozoic era when the Gondwana supercontinent fragmented. The Indian plate drifted northwards from the Southern Hemisphere and collided with the Eurasian plate, leading to the formation of the Himalayas. The Peninsular plateau is composed of ancient igneous and metamorphic rocks, making it a stable and earthquake-resistant region. It is the oldest landmass of India and contains major mineral resources. The Eastern and Western Ghats run parallel to the Bay of Bengal and the Arabian Sea, respectively.

question: What can happen if rocks are not weathered in the context of the movement of Earth's materials? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (07/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Mass movement would be more frequent
Soil fertility would improve
Erosion would be insignificant
Erosion would increase
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Erosion would be insignificant

Explanation:
Weathering breaks down rocks into smaller particles, providing the material necessary for erosion. If weathering does not occur, rocks remain solid and intact, making their transport by wind, water, or ice nearly impossible. Thus, the process of erosion would stop or become insignificant. Mass movements (such as landslides) also depend on weathering; without it, they would decrease, not increase. Soil fertility also requires weathering, as it releases minerals. Hence, in the absence of weathering, erosion would be insignificant.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which process becomes insignificant in the absence of weathering? → Erosion
☛ Weathering provides material for which process? → Erosion
☛ Without weathering, mass movement would be? → Less frequent
☛ Which process is essential for soil fertility? → Weathering
☛ What is the relationship between erosion and weathering? → Weathering supplies material for erosion

question: Which of the following best describes the public sector's role in the Indian economy during 1947–1991? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (07/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Dominant in core and heavy industries
Only limited to agriculture
Minimal presence
Focussed only on foreign trade
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Dominant in core and heavy industries

Explanation:
Between 1947 and 1991, India followed a socialist model where the public sector played a dominant role in the economy. The Industrial Policy Resolutions of 1948 and 1956 placed heavy industries under government control. Under Five-Year Plans, public sector undertakings (PSUs) were established in sectors like iron & steel, coal, power, and machinery. The government invested in infrastructure and capital-intensive industries to fill gaps left by the private sector. This was part of the import substitution and self-reliance strategy, making the public sector dominant in core and heavy industries.

question: The distribution of population in India is: (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (07/08/2025) Shift 1)

more in desert areas
denser in hilly regions
uneven, with variations across regions

question: Which state became the leading beneficiary of the Green Revolution in India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (07/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Bihar
Assam
Punjab
Odisha
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Punjab

Explanation:
The Green Revolution in India (1960-70s) benefited Punjab the most. This revolution involved the use of high-yielding variety seeds (HYV), chemical fertilizers, pesticides, and modern irrigation methods. Punjab's fertile soil, well-developed irrigation system, and progressive farmers made it the epicenter of the Green Revolution. As a result, Punjab became the largest producer of wheat and rice, significantly contributing to India's food security. The key architect of the Green Revolution in India was Dr. M.S. Swaminathan, while politically, Chief Minister Pratap Singh Kairon promoted it. Other options like Bihar, Assam, and Odisha had limited impact from the Green Revolution.

question: Which region of India is most suitable for tea cultivation due to its climate and soil? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (07/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Western Rajasthan
Deccan Plateau
Assam and North Bengal
Punjab and Haryana
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Assam and North Bengal

Explanation:

question: Which of the following factors best explains the formation of ox-bow lakes along river courses?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (07/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Sudden uplift of riverbeds by tectonic activity
Tectonic uplift disrupting the flow
Glacial retreat leaving depressions
Lateral erosion on the outer banks and deposition on the inner banks
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Lateral erosion on the outer banks and deposition on the inner banks

Explanation:
Ox-bow lakes form in the slow-moving parts of rivers where the river creates many meanders. When a river flows around a bend, centrifugal force causes the water to move faster on the outer bank, leading to lateral erosion which cuts into the bank. On the inner bank, the water slows down, causing deposition of sand and silt. Over time, the meander becomes more pronounced, and eventually the two ends come close together. During a flood, the river cuts a straight path through the narrow neck, and the meander is cut off, forming a horseshoe-shaped lake known as an ox-bow lake. This process is purely due to erosion and deposition, not tectonic activity, uplift, or glacial retreat. Therefore, lateral erosion on the outer banks and deposition on the inner banks best explains the formation of ox-bow lakes.

☛ What is the shape of an ox-bow lake? → Horseshoe-shaped

question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कारक नदी मार्गों के किनारे गोखुर झीलों के निर्माण की सबसे अच्छी व्याख्या करता है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (07/08/2025) Shift 2)
options_hi: विवर्तनिक गतिविधि द्वारा नदी तल का अचानक उत्थान
विवर्तनिक उत्थान से प्रवाह बाधित होना
हिमनदी पीछे हटने से गड्ढे बनना
बाहरी किनारों पर पार्श्व अपरदन और आंतरिक किनारों पर निक्षेपण
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है बाहरी किनारों पर पार्श्व अपरदन और आंतरिक किनारों पर निक्षेपण

Explanation:
गोखुर झीलों का निर्माण नदी के धीमी गति वाले भागों में होता है, जहाँ नदी बहुत सारे मोड़ बनाती है। जब नदी किसी मोड़ पर बहती है, तो अपकेंद्रीय बल के कारण पानी बाहरी किनारे से अधिक वेग से बहता है, जिससे वहाँ पार्श्व अपरदन (लैटरल इरोज़न) होता है और किनारा कट जाता है। दूसरी ओर, भीतरी किनारे पर पानी का वेग कम हो जाता है, जिससे वहाँ निक्षेपण (डिपॉज़िशन) होता है और रेत-मिट्टी जमा हो जाती है। समय के साथ, मोड़ और अधिक तीव्र हो जाता है, और अंततः दोनों सिरे पास आ जाते हैं। बाढ़ के दौरान, नदी सीधा रास्ता बना लेती है और मोड़ कटकर अलग हो जाता है, जो एक घोड़े की नाल के आकार की झील बनाता है, जिसे गोखुर झील या ऑक्स-बो झील कहते हैं। इस प्रक्रिया में विवर्तनिक गतिविधि, उत्थान या हिमनदी पीछे हटने जैसे कारक शामिल नहीं होते। अतः, बाहरी किनारों पर पार्श्व अपरदन और आंतरिक किनारों पर निक्षेपण ही गोखुर झीलों के निर्माण की सबसे अच्छी व्याख्या है।
